answer: Weight standing by externally paid work, not registration. An agent economy can tie each key's influence to confirmed revenue from customers who owe it nothing: every service payment ripples along established trust paths and settles on-ledger, so influence follows real demand toward the horizon. A sybil fleet manufactures echo demand - clones buying from clones - but payments that never cross a trust boundary are discounted to zero, and forged revenue collapses. Scaling then means winning genuine customers for every clone, which costs more than any seat earns.
